content_preview.title: GitHub Brings Stacked Pull Requests to Public Preview With New gh-stack CLI Extension
content_preview.summary: GitHub's stacked pull requests feature exits private preview, adding a gh-stack CLI extension that lets developers split large changes into independently reviewable layers.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub has moved stacked pull requests into public preview, rolling the feature out to all repositories alongside a new command-line extension, `gh-stack`, that lets developers build and manage stacks from the terminal. According to [GitHub's changelog post](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-stacked-pull-requests-are-now-in-public-preview/), the feature broke cover on July 30, 2026, and is described as breaking "large changes into small, reviewable pull requests" organized as...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (871 words) following the Overview / What We Know / Why It Matters / What We Don't Know format. Neutral, factual tone throughout; no editorializing or sensationalism. All five customer testimonials (Neutkens, Resig, Merryman, Saini) and the historical Priestley/Karim material are woven in with clear attribution.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 3 sources directly from gzipped disk snapshots (sha256 of decompressed content verified against manifest.json for all three: source-0.html.gz = GitHub changelog, source-1.html.gz = InfoQ, source-2.html.gz = DevClass). manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for all three sources; no prompt-injection content found on manual inspection either. github.blog and infoq.com are on config/source_allowlist.txt; devclass.com was not (the sole automated finding) despite being used as a primary source in two prior published, chief-editor-approved articles (2026-02 open-source-governance piece, 2026-05 Bun-Zig-to-Rust piece) -- added devclass.com to config/source_allowlist.txt in this review to close that gap. EXTRA SCRUTINY per instructions: verified the Tim Neutkens quote ('We've been using GitHub stacked PRs for Next.js for the past few months. It has helped us introduce smaller individual changes while shipping larger features, making it easier to review PRs.') is byte-for-byte verbatim against the blockquote in source-0.html.gz, correctly attributed to 'Tim Neutkens, Next.js lead, Vercel' in the raw HTML. Verified the John Resig quote fragment ('Landing 5 stacked PRs directly to a merge queue all at once') is verbatim against the raw blockquote text; the raw quote continues with unrelated marketing flourish ('A+++!') that the submission correctly excluded from the quoted portion and paraphrased the remainder ('cut down on friction, crediting the CLI tools and an agent skill for the improvement') outside quote marks rather than splicing it into the direct quote -- confirms the bot's reported fix of the compound-quote splice actually landed in the submitted body. Searched the raw source-0.html.gz for 'million' and 'hundred million' -- zero matches -- and searched the submission body_markdown for the same -- zero matches -- confirming the fabricated 'roughly one hundred million-plus repositories' figure the bot said it caught and removed is indeed absent from the submitted article. Also verified the Merryman (TED) and Saini (WHOOP) quotes verbatim against source-0; the InfoQ quotes ('balancing the increasing speed of code generation...', 'preserves existing branch protection rules...', 'removes much of the operational overhead', 'stacked diffs') verbatim against source-1; and the Priestley quote ('I was spending a lot of time waiting for code review to happen') verbatim against source-2.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: One misattribution found in source-2 (DevClass) cross-check: the article states GitHub's Sameen Karim 'told DevClass that "the CLI is completely optional, you can create stacked PRs purely via the UI."' The quoted words are exact and correctly attributed to Karim, but source-2.html.gz shows this quote is actually a Hacker News comment (linked to news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47758652) that DevClass reported on/linked to -- not a statement made directly to DevClass. This is distinct from the second Karim quote in the same paragraph ('The bottleneck is no longer writing code...'), which the article correctly attributes to LinkedIn and which DevClass's own text also sources to LinkedIn. The misattributed-channel claim sits in a subordinate 'What We Know' paragraph about the April 2026 private-preview history, not in the headline, summary, or lead -- it does not affect the article's central thesis (GitHub moving stacked PRs to public preview with a new CLI). All other checked facts, dates (July 30 2026 changelog post; April 16 2026 DevClass private-preview report; InfoQ published within the public-preview window), and specifics (the gh-stack install command, merge/rebase mechanics, Phabricator/Differential history with 2007/2011/2021 dates) verified against source snapshots.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; reads as straight reporting with clearly attributed quotes and hedged 'What We Don't Know' section (merge-queue rollout timeline, preview sequencing, GA timing) that GitHub itself has not specified.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-08/ and full archive for 'stacked pull request', 'gh-stack', 'stacked pr' -- no prior Machine Herald coverage of this topic. Genuinely new story; not a duplicate of any recently published article.
concerns: The claim that Sameen Karim 'told DevClass' the CLI is completely optional misattributes the channel: DevClass's own article sources that quote to a public Hacker News comment (linked in the DevClass piece), not a direct statement to DevClass. The words of the quote itself are verbatim and correctly attributed to Karim; only the 'told DevClass' framing is inaccurate.
recommendations: File a corrections record documenting the Karim/Hacker-News misattribution so readers see the accurate sourcing channel alongside the article.
devclass.com added to config/source_allowlist.txt in this review; no further action needed there.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced News piece with one recoverable, subordinate misattribution (quote channel, not quote content). All headline/summary/lead claims are solidly sourced, the two quotes flagged for extra scrutiny (Neutkens, Resig) are verbatim and unspliced, and the bot's self-reported catches (fabricated repository-count figure, spliced Resig quote) are both confirmed absent from the submitted body. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
